content:
We’re excited to share that by official invitation, the ByteDance Seed team participated in the IMO 2025, deploying our formal math reasoning system Seed Prover, based on Lean.

Over three days, Seed Prover solved 4 out of 6 problems and partially solved another, achieving a certified IMO score of 30 — equivalent to a silver medal :second_place: (scores: 2/7/7/7/7/0). Later, it went on to fully solve 5 problems with extended compute.

Seed Prover is built on Lean and trained via multi-stage reinforcement learning. It enables formal verification of math problems at scale by combining long-chain-of-thought reasoning, Lean feedback, and dynamic test-time compute strategies.

Highlights:

  • Full formal proofs for 5 IMO 2025 problems, available here:
    P1: p1.lean
    P2: p2_proof.pdf
    P3: p3.lean
    P4: p4.lean
    P5: p5.lean

  • Seed Prover uses three test-time inference modes:

    • Lightweight: up to 8 iterations, ~1 hour total compute

    • Medium: internal + external proof optimization, hours to days

    • Heavyweight: multi-day lemma/conjecture pool exploration (used for IMO 2025 P3/P4)

Benchmark results (vs. previous SOTA):

  • MiniF2F-valid: 100% (prev. 90.6%)

  • MiniF2F-test: 99.6% (prev. 92.2%)

  • PutnamBench: 331 proofs (prev. 64)

  • CombiBench: 30% (prev. 10%)

  • MiniCTX-v2: 81.8% (prev. 44.3%)

This work shows what’s possible when formal methods, LLMs, and scalable reasoning come together.

Big thanks to the IMO Committee for inviting us and validating the results, and to everyone in the community who contributed to Lean, mathlib, and the broader ecosystem.

Special thanks to @Zheng Yuan @ByronW @RexWang @Thomas Zhu for your support throughout the project :raised_hands:
